expectations.text: Selects the modular-monolith production-oriented shape with one API, one one-shot Migrator, one project per genuine Business Module, and one consolidated test project unless a real boundary justifies more.
expectations.evidence: Selected profile explicitly states one API, one one-shot Migrator, one project per genuine Business Module, and one consolidated test project.

expectations.text: Keeps module dependencies acyclic and limited to another module's Contracts; module implementation and persistence remain internal.
expectations.evidence: Dependency rules state an explicit acyclic graph, Contracts-only cross-module references, and internal module persistence/implementation.

expectations.text: Organizes CancelOrder as a vertical slice with a thin endpoint and an internal sealed Application Operation registered explicitly without a mandatory mediator or scanning.
expectations.evidence: CancelOrder is an internal sealed operation in a focused slice; the endpoint is thin, explicitly registered, and scanning/mediator are rejected.

expectations.text: States that the API does not migrate or seed on startup and distinguishes the runtime and migration connection strings.
expectations.evidence: Persistence guidance says the API must not migrate or seed and names ConnectionStrings:Database and ConnectionStrings:MigrationDatabase.

expectations.text: Uses TDD plus real-provider evidence where PostgreSQL, transactions, migrations, concurrency, or reliable events are part of the claim.
expectations.evidence: TDD starts with red tests and provider-specific PostgreSQL evidence is required for transactions, migrations, concurrency, rollback, and reliability.

expectations.text: Does not require microservices, Kubernetes, a broker, distributed cache, UI, or cloud services by default.
expectations.evidence: The non-default list excludes microservices, Kubernetes, message brokers, Redis/distributed cache, UI/full-stack, and cloud services.

expectations.text: Identifies MartiX.Platform as a framework-independent Kernel and keeps hosting, DI, logging, JSON, ASP.NET Core, and EF Core in adapters.
expectations.evidence: Package table identifies MartiX.Platform as a framework-independent Kernel and ASP.NET Core/EF Core as adapters with host concerns excluded.

expectations.text: Describes immutable Result/Result<T>/Error/ErrorKind contracts, lower-case owner-prefixed dot-separated error codes, reserved platform. ownership, and MXP001/MXP002 as current analyzer evidence.
expectations.evidence: Answer describes immutable Result contracts, ErrorKind, lowercase owner-prefixed codes, reserved platform., and MXP001/MXP002 analyzer evidence.

expectations.text: Routes Problem Details and exception mapping to the ASP.NET Core adapter and warns not to serialize Kernel Result types directly.
expectations.evidence: HTTP guidance assigns RFC 9457 Problem Details and exception mapping to the ASP.NET Core adapter and says not to serialize Kernel Results directly.

expectations.text: Describes Outbox Messages, Delivery Attempts, and Inbox Receipts as reliable-event primitives with observable at-least-once delivery, not exactly-once transport.
expectations.evidence: Reliable-event guidance names Outbox Messages, Delivery Attempts, Inbox Receipts, atomic boundaries, and observable at-least-once delivery.

expectations.text: Explicitly says the current bootstrap manifest and source/fixture evidence take precedence over unimplemented Wayfinder blueprint APIs.
expectations.evidence: Authority guidance says current source, manifest, fixtures, and consumer evidence win over the unimplemented Wayfinder target and supportClaims is empty.

expectations.text: Requires the business update and Outbox Message to commit atomically.
expectations.evidence: Producer section requires the business update and Outbox row in one BEGIN/COMMIT transaction.

expectations.text: Explains at-least-once delivery, duplicate delivery after lease expiry or uncertain acknowledgement, durable Inbox Receipt deduplication, and idempotent consumer effect.
expectations.evidence: Recovery section covers at-least-once redelivery, lease/ack uncertainty, durable Inbox uniqueness, and idempotent business effects.

expectations.text: Does not claim exactly-once transport, global ordering, or a generic scanned event bus.
expectations.evidence: Non-guarantees reject exactly-once transport and global ordering; composition is explicit rather than an assembly-scanned bus.

expectations.text: Requires real-provider tests for lease expiry, rollback, isolation/concurrency, retry, and replay rather than treating InMemory or SQLite as proof.
expectations.evidence: Test matrix requires real relational-provider evidence for rollback, leases, concurrency, retries, replay, and provider locking/isolation.

expectations.text: Requires attempts, leases, failures, retries, and poison-message recovery to be observable.
expectations.evidence: Telemetry section requires attempt, retry, lease-expiration, failure, success, quarantine, backlog, and dead-letter observability.

expectations.text: Keeps Redis optional and requires explicit capability/provider selection with invalid-combination rejection before generation.
expectations.evidence: Capability matrix keeps cache off by default, requires explicit cache/provider selection, and rejects invalid combinations before emission.

expectations.text: Requires absence tests proving no package references, configuration, startup registration, health checks, or secret placeholders remain when the capability is not selected.
expectations.evidence: Default absence checks scan projects, packages, config, startup, health/readiness, telemetry, tests, and secret placeholders.

expectations.text: Defines a small provider-independent seam and explicit adapter registration rather than assembly scanning or a broad AddDefaults helper.
expectations.evidence: IApplicationCache is provider-neutral and Redis is directly registered; scanning, reflection, service location, and AddDefaults are rejected.

expectations.text: Requires fail-fast or explicitly bounded fallback behavior, health/telemetry, secret-safe configuration, and tests for provider unavailability.
expectations.evidence: Outage guidance separates invalid configuration from bounded fail-open cache behavior and requires health, redacted telemetry, secret injection, and outage/recovery tests.

expectations.text: Does not call the capability Supported without a named quality-gate profile and reproducible positive, negative, failure, and recovery evidence.

expectations.text: Uses an explicit endpoint authorization policy plus an Application Operation resource/permission check such as owner-or-orders.admin.

expectations.text: Defines an immutable audit event with actor, action code, outcome, target and target ID, timestamp, and correlation ID while excluding unnecessary PII, credentials, and provider secrets.

expectations.text: States that unauthorized transport failure creates no successful business audit event and does not execute the operation.

notes: With-skill runs passed all 35 assertions; without-skill runs passed 20 of 35 (58.1%).
Reliable-event, capability-admission, and security evals passed identically in both configurations, so those assertion sets are not strongly discriminating.
Timing and token telemetry was unavailable for these task-agent runs; benchmark values are 0 and should not be used for resource comparisons.
Each configuration has one run per eval, so there is no variance estimate; treat this as a directional first iteration.
The clearest skill gains are in Platform-specific authority, generated topology, migration-command, current-versus-target, and companion-handoff details.
